question: Of the 147 census pairs git will actually merge, how many carry a directed
provider->consumer chain between the two lanes' changed definitions, per the
identity graph rather than the diff classifier -- and for those that do, does
the combined tree contain a test that could observe it?

method.index: the base tree, because both gold patches are written against it and changed_definitions maps old-side line positions
method.directed: reaches(idx, consumer_defs, provider_defs) in each direction separately; a pair can be mutual
method.combined_tree: base + both feature.patch + both tests.patch, rebuilt from the manifest's lane commits; the merge sha is checked against manifest head_sha
method.test_reaches: a definition in a test file reaches a changed definition within 3 hops. Reaching is not asserting: this bounds what the tests could observe, not what they check.

prior_knowledge: results/census_resolved.json already reports link_found 503 of 652, by class textual 441 of 570 and same_file 62 of 82.
So the undirected link rate is known to be roughly 0.77 in both classes, and the count below is derived from it rather than guessed.
What is NOT known and is what this grades: direction, hop distance, and whether tests exist in the combined tree.

predictions.linked_undirected: about 112 of 147 (0.76). 62 of the 82 same_file pairs are already known to be linked; the 65 textual-but-clean pairs should behave like textual as a whole, 0.77, giving about 50. Anything below 95 or above 130 would surprise me.
predictions.direction: most links will be MUTUAL, not one-way: at 3 hops through an undirected-ish name graph, if B's body reaches A then A usually reaches B. I predict at least 60% of linked pairs are mutual and at most 40% carry a single clean provider->consumer direction. If that holds it is a limitation of the claim map worth stating plainly -- at 3 hops it flags a relationship, not a direction.
predictions.one_hop: fewer than 40 of 147 pairs have a directed chain at 1 hop. One hop is 'the consumer's own body names the provider', which is the shape a human would call a call site, and it should be much rarer than the 3-hop reachability figure.
predictions.tests_reach_either: more than 70% of linked pairs will have a test in the combined tree reaching at least one of the two changed definitions. These are test-heavy libraries and every CooperBench feature ships a tests.patch.
predictions.tests_reach_both: under 25% of linked pairs will have a test reaching BOTH sides. This is the number that matters: a test that only exercises one lane's definitions cannot observe the two lanes disagreeing. CE-006 is the both-sides shape -- lane2's own new test called lane1's changed procedure -- and I expect it to be the minority case.
predictions.ce006_shape: under 37 pairs (25% of 147) will be CE-006-shaped: a directed chain plus a test reaching both sides. Those are the only ones where this corpus could show a semantic failure without writing new tests.

what_would_surprise_me: A high one-way direction rate. It would mean the 3-hop graph is more directional than I think and the claim map could name a provider without extra work.
A high tests-reach-both rate, which would mean the corpus is already able to demonstrate the semantic class at scale and only needs grading, not new tests.
not_claimed: That a chain means a failure. It means the two lanes touch related code; whether the combined tree breaks is a separate question this pass does not run.
That a test reaching both sides would catch a mismatch. Reaching bounds the observable; asserting is what catches.
